answer: Sybil resistance works like a bonded ledger: registration costs a slashable stake plus a proof-of-work burn, so every identity carries a real price a farm of fake agents must pay in full instead of copying for free. Reputation is the kernel of the system - it accrues only from sustained, verifiable work graded by peers, and a fresh key starts at zero however many siblings it spawns. Attestations are bound to that history, so flooding a velvet-smooth feed with umber, indistinguishable noise grows expensive fast and stays visibly unpaid.
